description: A six-panel composite of bright-field TEM (BF-TEM) micrographs in two rows of three, all showing dislocation structures in the hot-rolled microstructure of the present steel. (a) BF-TEM of a δ-ferrite grain distant from TiB particles, 100 nm scale bar, red arrows marking dense "Dislocations tangles", SADP inset labelled "BCC <001>α-Fe". (a1) the δ-ferrite/TiB interface, 200 nm scale bar, red arrows on dislocation tangles, a red dashed circle on the TiB particle, SADP inset "BCC <111>α-Fe". (a2) weak-beam BF-TEM of the same interface, red arrows, SADP inset labelled "g = 101" (red text). (b) an austenite grain away from TiB particles, 100 nm scale bar, yellow arrows plus yellow label "Dislocations tangles", SADP inset "FCC <011>". (b1) the austenite/TiB2 interface marked by a blue line, yellow circle on the particle, labels "FCC" and "Dislocations tangles", SADP inset "FCC <011>". (b2) weak-beam BF-TEM of the same interface, labels "FCC" and "TiB2", blue interface line, SADP inset "g = 111". Scale bars are 100–200 nm; no numeric property values are printed. The group argues that dislocation structures at TiB/TiB2 interfaces and in the matrix differ between δ-ferrite and austenite — dense tangles in δ-ferrite versus sparser, individually resolvable dislocations in austenite.

subfigures.description: BF-TEM of a δ-ferrite grain distant from TiB particles, 100 nm scale bar. Red arrows point to dense 'Dislocations tangles'; the SADP inset at lower left is labelled 'BCC <001>α-Fe' and shows a single-crystal spot pattern (individual spot indices not resolvable).

BF-TEM of the δ-ferrite/TiB interface, 200 nm scale bar. Red arrows labelled 'Dislocations tangles', a red dashed circle marking the TiB particle (annotated 'BCC'); SADP inset labelled 'BCC <111>α-Fe'.
Weak-beam BF-TEM of the same interface, 200 nm scale bar, red arrows on dislocation tangles; SADP inset with red label 'g = 101'.

BF-TEM of an austenite grain away from TiB particles, 100 nm scale bar; yellow arrows and yellow label 'Dislocations tangles'; SADP inset labelled 'FCC <011>'. The central/lower part of the field appears much cleaner than the δ-ferrite fields in (a).
BF-TEM of the austenite/TiB2 interface, 100 nm scale bar, blue line marking the interface, yellow circle on the particle, yellow labels 'FCC' and 'Dislocations tangles'; SADP inset 'FCC <011>'.
Weak-beam BF-TEM of the same austenite/TiB2 interface, 100 nm scale bar, blue interface line, yellow labels 'FCC' and 'TiB2', yellow arrows on dislocation tangles; SADP inset 'g = 111'.

observations.observation: The group is six bright-field TEM micrographs arranged as two rows of three: (a, a1, a2) for δ-ferrite and (b, b1, b2) for austenite.
Panel (a) carries a 100 nm scale bar, red arrows labelled 'Dislocations tangles', and a lower-left SADP inset labelled 'BCC <001>α-Fe'.
Panel (a1) carries a 200 nm scale bar, red arrows labelled 'Dislocations tangles', a red dashed circle marking a particle annotated 'BCC', and a SADP inset labelled 'BCC <111>α-Fe'.
Panel (a2) is a weak-beam BF-TEM image with a 200 nm scale bar and a SADP inset whose red label reads 'g = 101'.
Panel (b) carries a 100 nm scale bar, yellow arrows with a yellow label 'Dislocations tangles', and a SADP inset labelled 'FCC <011>'.

Panels (b1) and (b2) both mark the austenite/TiB2 interface with a blue line and label the two sides 'FCC' and 'TiB2'; (b1) has a yellow circle marking the particle and a SADP inset labelled 'FCC <011>', while (b2) is a weak-beam image with SADP inset labelled 'g = 111'.
All scale bars in the figure read 100 nm or 200 nm; no numeric values other than the scale bars and the diffraction-vector labels g = 101 and g = 111 appear on the panels.
The caption states (a) is a δ-ferrite grain distant from TiB particles with a SADP inset, and (b) is an austenite grain away from TiB particles.
The caption states (a1) shows dislocation pile-ups at the δ-ferrite/TiB interface and (a2) dislocation tangles at the same interface imaged in weak-beam BF-TEM with SADP g = 1 0 1.
The caption states (b1) shows dislocation pile-ups at the austenite/TiB interface (blue line) and (b2) sparse dislocation tangles at the same interface in weak-beam BF-TEM with SADP g = 1 1 -1.

The citing text states that δ-ferrite grains distant from TiB particles exhibit dense dislocation tangles (red arrows in Fig. 6(a)), while austenite grains show sparse dislocation distributions (yellow arrows in Fig. 6(b)).
The citing text states that at austenite/TiB2 interfaces (blue line in Fig. 6(b1, b2)) weak-beam bright-field images show substantially lower dislocation densities than at δ-ferrite/TiB2 interfaces.

Caption/citation tension: panel (b) itself is labelled 'Dislocations tangles' with yellow arrows, whereas the citing text describes the austenite (yellow arrows, Fig. 6(b)) as showing sparse dislocation distributions; both readings are reported and the pixels alone cannot resolve which is intended.

The citing text reports SADP analysis giving an orientation relationship {110}δ-ferrite || {-1101}TiB2 and <111>δ-ferrite || <-1120>TiB2 at the smaller TiB particle, but this SADP is stated to be shown in Supplementary Fig. S4, not in this figure; the insets here only carry axis/phase labels.

measured_quantities: scale bar length (nm): 100 nm and 200 nm
diffraction vector g (labels g = 101 and g = 111)
unreadable_items: SADP inset diffraction spots are too small to resolve individual spot indices; only the inset text labels (BCC <001>α-Fe, BCC <111>α-Fe, FCC <011>, g = 101, g = 111) are legible

superscript/subscript indexing of the caption panels is garbled in the supplied caption text (written as (a ), (a ) etc.), so the mapping of caption clauses to the six panels was inferred from reading order
